bad.title: “I don’t like it” names nothing
bad.text: Kai can’t tell if it’s the amount, the fields or the button.

bad.title: “Cluttered” with no goal behind it
bad.text: The screen has four parts. Cluttered for whom, and for what task?

bad.title: The designer has to ask
bad.text: With nothing to act on, Kai defends the design or changes something at random.

good.title: Starts from the person’s goal
good.text: Fast and without mistakes, so every point after it can be judged against that.

good.title: The problem, with its cost
good.text: One typo sends €250 to a stranger. Kai sees why it matters.

good.title: One reply, one clear change
good.text: Kai knows what to fix and why: a name check before Send.

bad.title: A fix with no reason
bad.text: Bigger for what? Kai can only do it or argue, since no problem is named.

bad.title: Checkout sits below six suggestions
bad.text: People have to scroll the bag to find it, and a bigger button stays down there.

good.title: The problem and its cause
good.text: People scroll past six items and give up, so any fix can be checked against that.

good.title: A fix the problem points to
good.text: Moving Checkout under the bag solves it, and the button doesn’t need to grow.

bad.title: Version 0.1, still dashed boxes
bad.text: The order of the questions is still open, so the details may not survive.

bad.title: Padding notes on a sketch
bad.text: 12 or 16 px won’t matter if the questions change order tomorrow.

bad.title: Brand color before the flow works
bad.text: Nobody asks yet whether dates should come before the city.

good.title: Kai says what feedback helps
good.text: Direction, not polish, with one concrete question to answer.

good.title: Ben answers the question asked
good.text: He argues from what people know first, which could change the whole sketch.

good.title: Lea adds an idea, not a pixel
good.text: “Anywhere” as a choice serves people who know only their dates.

bad.title: Ana leads with her own note
bad.text: The talk is about slot size before Kai says a word.

bad.title: Kai just agrees
bad.text: His own doubt about the date never comes up.

bad.title: People still book the wrong day
bad.text: The problem Kai suspected ships, because nobody asked him.
bad.wait: Press Two weeks later to see this.

good.title: Ana asks before she speaks
good.text: What works and what worries Kai, so his read comes out first.

good.title: Kai’s doubt comes out
good.text: The date set to Today, a problem Ana had missed.

good.title: Two fixes, one from each
good.text: Make the date stand out and the slots bigger. Neither review alone had both.
good.wait: Press Write down the next steps to see this.

bad.title: Three findings, all predictions
bad.text: Each one is what a reviewer expected to go wrong. Nobody has tried the flow yet.

bad.title: The real problem ships
bad.text: 4 in 10 people leave at Phone number, a step the review never flagged.
bad.wait: Press Fix and ship to see this.

good.title: The same three findings
good.text: The review is still the starting point, but not the last word.

good.title: Five people reorder the list
good.text: Phone number stopped 3 of 5, and nobody noticed the two Continue buttons.
good.wait: Press Watch 5 people to see this.

good.title: Fixes go where people struggled
good.text: The phone step and the password rules come first, and far fewer people leave.
good.wait: Press Watch 5 people, then Fix and ship, to see this.

bad.title: One reviewer, 4 of 11
bad.text: A single person misses most problems, and the team can’t tell which.

bad.title: Back empties the basket, unseen
bad.text: One of seven problems nobody found. It ships as it is.
bad.wait: Press Show what was missed to see this.

good.title: The count climbs with each reviewer
good.text: From 4 of 11 to 7, 9 and 10 as reviewers join.

good.title: Each reviewer finds different things
good.text: Reviewer 2 adds three problems Reviewer 1 never saw.
good.wait: Press Add a reviewer to see this.

good.title: Past four, little is new
good.text: Reviewer 4 adds only one problem, so a fifth would add little.
good.wait: Press Add a reviewer three times to see this.

bad.title: The list starts with icon sizes
bad.text: The order they were found in says nothing about how much they hurt.

bad.title: The worst problem is fourth
bad.text: People can’t pay, and it looks no more urgent than a typo.

bad.title: Three fixes, payments still broken
bad.text: Icon sizes, the typo and the blurry logo are done, and people still can’t pay.
bad.wait: Press Fix the first three to see this.

good.title: Severity 4 at the top
good.text: Failed card payments stop people from ordering, so they come first.

good.title: Cosmetic issues sink to 1
good.text: Icon sizes, the typo and the logo can wait without anyone losing an order.

good.title: The first three are the ones that hurt
good.text: Payments, the emptied basket and the hidden fee get fixed. The cosmetic ones wait.
good.wait: Press Fix the first three to see this.

bad.title: “Everything else passes” is a guess
bad.text: A mock can’t show focus, timing or errors, so nobody checked them.

bad.title: Two failures show up after release
bad.text: Focus stays behind the dialog and the progress never moves. Neither was drawn.
bad.wait: Press Ship it to see this.

good.title: The gaps get their own heading
good.text: Next to the findings, so a clean review can’t pass for a full one.

good.title: Each gap becomes a test
good.text: Focus, timing, errors and screen readers each get checked in the running build.

good.title: Two of four fail, before release
good.text: Focus behind the dialog and the stuck progress get fixed while it’s still cheap.
good.wait: Press Check them in the build to see this.

bad.title: Four tools with no names
bad.text: Crop, Light, Color and Filters are bare icons, so people guess.

bad.title: Two rules that pull apart
bad.text: Hide the toolbar, label every tool. A checklist can’t say which one wins.

bad.title: Every box ticked, still no answer
bad.text: The labels exist, but on a toolbar nobody can see.
bad.wait: Tick both rules to see this.

good.title: Labeled tools while editing
good.text: Crop, Light, Color and Filters each have a name, so nobody guesses.

good.title: Both principles asked about one goal
good.text: Quick edits on a phone, so the two questions point to the same design.

good.title: Tap the photo to see it whole
good.text: The toolbar hides only when people want a clear look.

bad.title: Six pale icons, nothing else
bad.text: Light gray looks calm but is hard to see, and none says what it opens.

bad.title: Notifications hides behind a stack icon
bad.text: People try the icons one by one until they land on it.

good.title: Six names in full-strength text
good.text: The grid looks almost the same, and people read their way to the setting.

good.title: Notifications on the first try
good.text: The label is the essential part, so it stays.

bad.title: A countdown that starts over
bad.text: At zero it resets to 4:59, so the urgency is made up.

bad.title: Audiobooks ticked for people
bad.text: +€3 a month is added unless people notice and untick it.

bad.title: €9.99 in the smallest, palest print
bad.text: The price after 3 months is the hardest thing on the screen to read.

good.title: The later price in plain text
good.text: €9.99 after 3 months sits right under the price, at full size.

good.title: Audiobooks starts unticked
good.text: It’s there for people who want it, and nobody pays for it by accident.

good.title: The button says what people pay
good.text: Tick the add-on and it changes to €7.99 today, before anyone commits.
